acceptance: A write that exceeds the client timeout can be retried with the same operation id and reports the original outcome.
The timeout message names how to reconcile.
Measured p95 latency of take and finish recorded before and after.
Retrying the same `context_append` with the same operation id does not append twice.
The cause of slow calls under host load is identified and written on this item.
BenchBox vendors the released tractable wheel under `_project/scripts/vendor/`, and a restarted tractable-mcp reports that version from `get_instructions`.
context:
BenchBox tracker store: BenchBox-dev/BenchBox branch todo-state. The host also had intermittent GitHub network drops the same day, which may explain the latency.

2026-11-17, merged from tractable-mcp-request-timeouts-20261112 (dropped as duplicate). Additional evidence: three occurrences on 2026-11-12 under heavy host load (load average 8-37, swap above 90%): a `list_items(text=...)` read, and two `update_item(context_append=...)` writes, each 'Request timeout after 30000ms ... the request outcome is unknown'; both writes had landed. Added acceptance: retrying the same `context_append` with the same operation id does not append twice, and the timeout cause under load (Git fetch or push to the state branch, lock contention, other) is identified and written here. Guardrail: do not raise the client timeout so far that a hung server blocks a session.

2026-11-16 recurrence: a take/update/finish sequence for site-docs-cli-contract-changes-20261113 hit the client 30 s timeout; the finish had landed, and a retried take was refused with E_STATE (item done). Reconciled by reading state back.

2026-11-17 review note: the fix belongs in the tractable repository (joeharris76/tractable); BenchBox picks it up by bumping the vendored wheel (_project/scripts/vendor, currently 1.1.1) and restarting tractable-mcp. Guardrail: do not raise the client timeout to hide slow calls.

Decision gate: first find where the time goes under load (Git fetch or push of the state branch, lock contention, or other) from timed server logs; choose idempotent operation-id replay, a faster write path, or both, based on that measurement, and record why. Item guardrails: no client timeout raised to hide slow calls; a retried write never applies twice; no change to the state-branch format without a schema version bump. Verification rubric: pass = the five acceptance points, with p95 take and finish latency before and after measured on the same host load, and a test that replays one operation id for take, finish and context_append. Fail = any duplicate append or double-applied finish on retry.

Owner decision 2026-11-17: in scope this round: fix upstream in joeharris76/tractable, release, then bump the vendored wheel in BenchBox and restart tractable-mcp.

2026-11-17 recurrence with a duplicate: five tracker writes issued close together from one session all hit the 30 s client timeout. All landed. One `context_append` on ci-artifact-downloads-single-attempt-20261117, retried after its timeout, was applied twice (the first attempt landed after the read-back showed it missing); the duplicate was removed by rewriting the context field. This is the double-apply the acceptance forbids, seen live. Until fixed, agents should issue tracker writes one at a time and wait at least 25 s before reading back a timed-out write. description:
Observed twice on 2026-11-12 against the BenchBox state store:
- `finish` on benchbox-lock-theseus-review-format-release-a-20261110 returned 'MCP failure … stage: receive, failure: timeout … Request timeout after 30000ms … the request outcome is unknown'. A later list_items showed the item done.
- `take` on theseus-review-minimize-superseded-20261110 timed out the same way. The item stayed open and unclaimed, and a retry took it.
In both cases the client cannot tell whether the write landed. A blind retry of finish would be refused or would double-apply, and a blind retry of take could fail with E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS if the first had landed. Agents have to read the state back by hand.
Work (tractable product; owner decides where it is fixed):
- Return the operation id before the slow part, or make the MCP write timeout longer than the state-branch push time.
- Make every write idempotent under a client-supplied operation id, so a retry with the same id is safe.
- Document the reconcile step (`tractable recover --op-id`, or show_item) in the timeout message.
Guardrails: no hand edits of the state branch; changes go through the tractable repository's own review.
